I would like to warmly thank the entire team at the veterinary clinic for the exceptional care they provided to my dog, Indie.

After several months of sneezing, reverse sneezing, and nasal discharge, they took the time to thoroughly investigate her condition. Thanks to a CT scan and a comprehensive dental examination, they identified erosive rhinitis of dental origin with dental abscesses, a condition that finally explained all her symptoms.

They also discovered acute hepatitis, immediately hospitalized her, started her on an IV drip, and monitored her closely. Throughout her hospitalization, I received regular calls for updates, which was incredibly reassuring.

The entire team always took the time to answer my questions, explain the tests, blood work results, and treatments.

I would especially like to thank Dr. Benjamin Perret for his professionalism, availability, and dedication.

When you entrust your pet to someone, you hope they will be treated like a member of the family. That's exactly how I felt throughout this entire process.

Thanks to their responsiveness, expertise, and compassion, Indie now has every chance of continuing her recovery in the best possible conditions.

A huge thank you to the whole team.

I would like to share my experience as a foreign pet owner to help others make an informed decision.

The principal vet examined my 5-year-old dog, whose teeth I brush regularly. During the consultation, I was advised to schedule a dental procedure costing more than €500, including tooth extraction. The vet presented himself as a dental specialist and mentioned that payment in instalments would be possible if cost was a concern.

What concerned me was the sense of urgency. I was strongly encouraged to have the procedure performed within the next few days, and when I declined, I was encouraged again to schedule it for the following week.

Given the cost and the urgency, I decided to seek second and third opinions from two other veterinary clinics. Both veterinarians independently informed me that the tooth extraction was not necessary at this stage and that my dog's dental condition did not justify such an intervention.

Based on these conflicting professional opinions, I chose not to proceed with the recommended treatment. I would encourage other pet owners, especially foreigners who may be unfamiliar with the local veterinary system, to seek a second opinion before agreeing to costly or urgent procedures.

After many hours, she made an appointment elsewhere and insisted on picking up her dog. Before letting her leave, the employee injected her with morphine, "to prevent her from suffering during the trip!" She then died on the way to the other vet!
